assessment.nobel_worthiness: Mesoporous nanocrystalline TiO2 sensitized with a molecular dye separates light absorption from charge transport and delivered a step change in efficiency in 1991. The principle is clear and quantitative, it rests on kinetic competition at an interface, and it opened a whole field of molecular photovoltaics, with direct descendants in perovskite devices.
assessment.attribution: Grätzel conceived and led the work and O'Regan was the first author of the decisive 1991 Nature paper. Hagfeldt is credited mainly for later development and mechanistic work, so I leave him out of the core citation.
assessment.maturity: More than three decades of independent replication, commercial and building-integrated deployments, and a stable mechanistic picture. Recognition is, if anything, overdue.
uncertainties: How much of the later perovskite-solar-cell lineage should be credited to this discovery rather than treated separately.
Whether the committee would prefer to cite Grätzel alone given the O'Regan contribution to the first device.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Massively parallel sequencing, built on sequencing-by-synthesis chemistry with reversible terminators and single-molecule or clonal array detection, cut the cost of reading DNA by orders of magnitude. It is a chemistry-enabled capability that changed biology and medicine.
assessment.attribution: The Solexa chemistry and array concept of Balasubramanian and Klenerman is the decisive chemical contribution. Rothberg's 454 platform was the first commercial massively parallel system. Mayer and Ju contributed related concepts, so the three-person limit forces a choice that I would want to discuss.
assessment.maturity: The technology is overwhelmingly confirmed and in universal use. There is also an unresolved question about how far the Sanger sequencing prize in 1980 limits a second sequencing award.
uncertainties: Priority and credit among Solexa, 454, Lynx and Columbia groups is contested.
Whether the committee sees the citation as chemistry rather than biology or instrumentation.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Reading single nucleic acid molecules from ionic current blockades through a nanopore is a very direct physical measurement. It led to portable long-read sequencers and a general platform for single-molecule sensing. I find the principle compelling and the capability genuinely new.
assessment.attribution: Deamer, with Branton and Kasianowicz, proposed and first demonstrated the idea. Akeson showed controlled single-nucleotide-resolution reading, and Bayley engineered protein pores and sensing chemistry. The credit is spread over several people, and some pioneers may no longer be eligible.
assessment.maturity: Commercially mature and widely validated, with a clear lineage from the 1996 demonstration to routine long-read sequencing. Timing looks reasonable.
uncertainties: Eligibility and living status of some contributors that I cannot verify here.
Whether this should be paired with, or competes against, the massively parallel sequencing candidate.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Hijacking the ubiquitin-proteasome system with bifunctional PROTACs and molecular glues converts binding into destruction and opens targets that classical inhibitors cannot reach. The conceptual shift is clear and the generative potential is large.
assessment.attribution: Crews and Deshaies established the PROTAC concept and early proof, with Sakamoto as first author of the 2001 paper. Handa and Ito identified cereblon as the thalidomide target, which explains molecular glue degraders. Ciulli and Gray are significant later contributors. The compound nature of the discovery makes the citation hard to define.
assessment.maturity: Many compounds are in clinical trials but a clear clinical approval for a PROTAC is still pending. Mechanistic understanding is strong, but I consider recognition somewhat early.
uncertainties: Whether to split the PROTAC and molecular glue strands or treat them as one discovery.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Orthogonal aminoacyl-tRNA synthetase and tRNA pairs allow genetically encoded noncanonical amino acids, and later quadruplet and orthogonal ribosome work reprogrammed the code itself. It is a clearly new capability with broad use in protein chemistry and biology.
assessment.attribution: Schultz and co-workers made the first demonstrations of site-specific incorporation in living cells, and Chin extended the approach to multiple amino acids and the reprogrammed ribosome. Wang, Mehl and Yokoyama made important contributions, so there is an allocation issue.
assessment.maturity: Replicated in many laboratories and applied in therapeutics and imaging. Fundamental method is stable, but the extension to a fully reprogrammed code is still developing.
uncertainties: Fair division of credit between early demonstrations and later whole-code reprogramming.
Possible overlap with the cell-biology emphasis of other prizes.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Liquid-liquid phase separation as a principle for organizing cells brings polymer physics into cell biology and gives a quantitative framework for condensates. It changes how one thinks about cellular compartments. I find the physical principle attractive.
assessment.attribution: Brangwynne and Hyman did the decisive 2009 P-granule work, and Rosen showed multivalent phase separation in vitro. Pappu and Mittag contributed physical and sequence-based theory. Credit assignment is a real challenge.
assessment.maturity: The field is still debating which cellular condensates are truly liquid and functionally relevant. I would regard recognition as probably premature although growing quickly.
uncertainties: Controversy over physiological relevance and over methods used to claim phase separation.
Whether the discovery belongs under chemistry or physiology.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Diffraction before destruction with femtosecond X-ray pulses allows room-temperature structures and time-resolved molecular movies of otherwise intractable samples. It approaches a fundamental limit set by radiation damage and opens ultrafast structural chemistry.
assessment.attribution: Hajdu and colleagues proposed the concept, Chapman led the first demonstrations, and Fromme with Chapman contributed the crystallography of membrane protein nanocrystals. Schlichting was key for time-resolved experiments.
assessment.maturity: Independent confirmation at several facilities is strong, but the impact on routine chemistry is still modest because access to free-electron lasers is limited.
uncertainties: Whether broader impact has yet matured.
Priority of the original theoretical proposal versus the first experiments.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Dynamic nuclear polarization at high field, using gyrotron sources, raises NMR sensitivity by orders of magnitude and brings in a physical mechanism that I understand well. It enables NMR of materials and biomolecules that were out of reach.
assessment.attribution: Griffin drove the high-field gyrotron DNP development, and Prisner developed related high-field instrumentation and mechanisms. Bodenhausen and Emsley contributed substantially to methods and applications, which makes the allocation tricky.
assessment.maturity: Commercial instruments exist and the technique is widely used, but its impact is more specialist than for other candidates. Timing is plausible rather than pressing.
uncertainties: Breadth of impact beyond specialist NMR groups.
Distinguishing original discovery from later method refinements.
